records.summary: Crime and faction mechanics simulate Noir City's evolving power dynamics.
◦ Join guilds like the Adventurer Guild or Merchant Guild for exclusive missions, discounts, and legal protection.
While not directly "government," guilds and corporations are quasi-governmental entities within the empireʼs structure.
Joining a Guild •Membership costs: MC 1,000–MC 2,000/year. •Benefits include access to protected trade routes, exclusive missions, and Influence bonuses.
This system rewards specific, significant contributions to the empire or its goals. Influence is earned through deeds, not wealth, and cannot be traded, purchased, or inherited.

◦ Influence Points are tracked within guilds and used to access guild-exclusive resources, rank advancement, and specialized tools. ◦ Guild-specific influence cannot be transferred between guilds, ensuring it reflects dedication to a particular cause.

•Cultural Basis: Clans and corporations are deeply intertwined. Members of goblin clans often display tattoos or bioluminescent marks denoting their corporate allegiances or ancestral lineage. •Implications: These marks may grant privileges in certain areas, like access to restricted zones, or could spark rivalries when encountering members of competing factions.

•Cultural Basis: Drawing from influences like the Rakuuta, the Guild of Mentors offers guidance to young goblins or adventurers starting their journeys. This mentorship is both professional and personal. •Implications: Mentors earn prestige for their proteges' successes, and mentees must uphold their mentors' reputation. This fosters strong bonds but can also create rivalries between mentor lineages.

1.Corporate Nobility (High-Class Elites) •CEOs, high-ranking executives, and corporate board members. •Directly influence imperial policy and control vast economic resources. •Wealth is not just measured in credits but in control over industries, stock holdings, and corporate power. •The most powerful hold Imperial Influence Credits, allowing them to bypass certain laws and negotiate directly with the throne. 2.High-Tier Wealth Holders (Powerful Entrepreneurs, Investors, & High-Ranking Officials) •Not part of mandated corporations but own major businesses, tech patents, or trade routes. •May act as independent governors of certain realities, operating under corporate partnerships. •Major adventurers, guild leaders, and influential merchants may reach this tier. 3.Corporate Middle-Class (Employees, Professionals, & Independent Traders) •The largest social group, consisting of corporate employees, skilled professionals, researchers, and managers. •Most receive corporate-sponsored housing, medical care (via Karma Ceutrica), and travel subsidies. •Some choose independent businesses or work in unregulated zones, hoping to break into higher wealth brackets. 4.Lower-Class & Unstable Workers (Gig Economy & Unstable Employment) •Those without permanent corporate employment must rely on freelance work, adventuring, or black-market trade. •Often live in high-density housing, relying on cheap automation and public resource hubs for survival. •Can survive through guild affiliations, independent markets, or scavenging the frontier. 5.The Disconnected & Unregistered (Frontier Workers, Outlaws, & Those in Unregulated Zones) •Individuals living outside imperial oversight, either due to choice or circumstance.
